cr_data.provenance:
1918–1986: Georgia O'Keeffe (1887–1986), New York/Abiquiú; the work remained in the artist's possession until her death 
 
1986–1995: Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation, Abiquiú, in the artist's estate, acquired by inheritance from the artist 
 
Since 1995: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München, donation from the Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation, Abiquiú 
(Source: Lenbachhaus, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1946. . . . On backing: A.S. writing, 'Series I, No. 4' [recorded incorrectly] 1918 By Georgia O'Keeffe Back: O'K: 'Series I, No. 4,' 1918" [second inscription not verified]. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 14. Completed after June move to New York. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication lists medium as 'Oil on canvas', Lenbachhaus lists it as 'Öl auf Faserplatte' (Oil on fiberboard). (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Lenbachhaus, 2025)

description: A central form that resembles layers of multicolored, draped fabric spirals in on itself. The form is made of pink, orange, blue, and green layers and expands outward toward the bottom of the composition. Behind the shape is a textured background in shades of red, pale blue, and white.
